approach: At dispatch, after the disk gates and before the producer brief is built, `Athena::dispatch` (crates/athena-core/src/run/mod.rs ~line 898) calls a new `snapshot::write(git, head, <state>/jobs/<id>/evidence)`. It copies `records/` at `head`, a merged `landings/` (the tree's plus the `athena/records` tip's, the same two sources `Records::load` uses), and a `history.json` (base commit plus the last 200 first-parent commits: hash, commit time, subject, trailers). It then locks the directory read-only, root-proof, with the write bits plus `chattr +i` and a write probe that fails the dispatch if the lock does not hold. `Records::load` is split so it and a new `Records::load_dir` share one `from_parts` assembly. That makes records read from the snapshot and from git go through the same code, so the throughput computation is untouched and its text matches. New `producer_brief_with_evidence` and `verifier_brief_with_evidence` (the old functions delegate with None, so no struct literal changes) add an "Evidence snapshot" section only when a path is given. The stored briefs show `<state>/jobs/<id>/evidence`. The text sent to the agent has the real path substituted, so no machine path is committed. The agent hook gets a read-only exemption: `Policy` gains `evidence: Option<PathBuf>` (serde default), set for producer and verifier only. `HookSpec` gains `read_dirs`, which the Claude driver passes as `--add-dir`. `athena status --snapshot <dir>` is handled in `main.rs` before `open()`, so it needs no repository. It calls `snapshot::status(dir)`, which prints job counts, a history summary and the unchanged `Throughput::text()`.

decisions.choice: Throughput parity comes from one shared assembly path: `Records::load` and `Records::load_dir` both call a new `Records::from_parts(RecordSet, landing files)`. `Throughput::compute` is not touched.
decisions.reason: `Throughput::compute(&Records)` reads only `Records`, including `records.landings` (status.rs ~929, `landing_record_time`). Identical records give identical text. One assembly path means the snapshot cannot drift from git. Criterion 7 forbids changing the throughput computation.

rejected.option: A second parser for snapshot files
rejected.why: It could drift from `Records::load` and break the identical-text requirement.

rejected.option: Rebuild a git repository from the snapshot and call `Athena::status`
rejected.why: `Athena::status` needs an Athena, the registry, config and code-health. The command must work with no repo or records/ in the current directory.

decisions.choice: The snapshot lives at `<state>/jobs/<id>/evidence` (a sibling of `work` and `live`). `snapshot::write` copies `records/`, `landings/` and `history.json`, then locks it. `lock` clears write bits, tries `chattr +i`, and probes by creating a file and opening an existing one for write. If either probe succeeds it unlocks and returns an error, and dispatch fails before the prediction commit, so nothing is committed.
decisions.reason: This mirrors `Snapshot::lock` in athena-git/src/snapshot.rs (lines 154-197), which is root-proof and already needed by the verifier's snapshot. Removal already works: `pin::remove_tree` calls `athena_git::snapshot::unlock_dir` before `remove_dir_all` (pin.rs 221-229), so `clean_job` and `JobWorktree` clean it up.

rejected.why: Root bypasses them. The behavior-evidence default requires a protection that holds for root.
It needs a git `Snapshot` value. A plain `lock_dir` in athena-core avoids touching a file outside the expected set; `unlock_dir` is reused.

rejected.option: On lock failure, warn and continue
rejected.why: The brief would say read-only for something that is not. Dispatch fails instead, as the verifier lock already does.

decisions.choice: The stored brief carries the placeholder `<state>/jobs/<id>/evidence`. The text sent to the agent has that exact string replaced by the real path. `brief_sha256` is the hash of the stored brief.
decisions.reason: The producer brief is committed verbatim (`brief-producer.md`, run/mod.rs 979), and the verifier brief is stored with the diff elided (verification.rs 179-182). The `<state>` placeholder is already the redactor's name for the state root (lib.rs `redactor`). Nothing recomputes `brief_sha256`; I grepped for it.

rejected.option: Put the real path in the stored brief
rejected.why: It commits a machine path (the public default).

rejected.option: A redactor pass over the stored brief
rejected.why: The hash would no longer match the stored text.

decisions.choice: Briefs gain `producer_brief_with_evidence(inputs, Option<&str>)` and `verifier_brief_with_evidence(inputs, plan, Option<&str>, inline_diff)`. `producer_brief` and `verifier_brief_with_plan` delegate with None. The frames (PRODUCER_FRAME, VERIFIER_FRAME) are not edited.
decisions.reason: There are about 12 `ProducerInputs` and `VerifierInputs` struct literals, in briefs.rs tests and reading.rs:5810; a new field would touch them all. The producer and verifier prompt sets are at 1257 of 1300 and 1298 of 1300 tokens (system-facts), so a frame edit risks `system_facts_budgets_match_computed`. Briefs sit outside those budgets.

rejected.option: A new `evidence` field on both input structs
rejected.why: It forces edits to every literal for no gain.

rejected.option: Put the instruction in the frames
rejected.why: It pushes the token budgets over.

decisions.choice: The agent hook change is `Policy.evidence: Option<PathBuf>` with `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`. `confine` gets a `read_extra` argument. A resolved path (symlinks followed) under the canonical evidence dir passes only when `write` is false. `agent_spec` sets it for Producer and Verifier only, and only when the dir exists. `HookSpec.read_dirs` makes the Claude driver add `--add-dir`.
decisions.reason: `athena-cli/src/hooks.rs::pre_tool_use` deserializes `Policy` from the file, so a defaulted optional field needs no change there and old policy files still parse. Reads, Grep and Glob, and `ls`-style arguments get the exemption. Writes and redirects never do. `cargo run -- status --snapshot <dir>` already passes: cargo arguments after the subcommand are not path-confined (policy.rs 623-652).

rejected.option: A symlink to the evidence inside the working copy
rejected.why: `confine` canonicalizes and would deny it, and it puts something in the candidate tree.

rejected.option: Allow any sibling `evidence` directory of the root by convention
rejected.why: It is implicit and weak. An explicit, canonicalized field is checkable.

rejected.option: Copy the evidence into the working copy
rejected.why: Out of scope: records/ must stay out of the producer's working copy.

decisions.choice: history.json is `{"base": <head>, "commits": [{hash, committed_at, subject, trailers}]}` from a new `Git::log_first_parent(rev, limit)` (athena-git/src/lib.rs). It uses `git log --first-parent -n200` with `%H`, `%cI`, `%s` and `%(trailers:only,unfold)`, parsed like `log_history`.
decisions.reason: The existing `Git::log_history` (lib.rs 905) has only the short hash and a `YYYY-MM-DD` date, and no trailers. The brief asks for hash, commit time, subject and trailers.

rejected.why: It lacks commit time and trailers, and it appends changed paths.

decisions.choice: The status view is a smaller `SnapshotView` (snapshot dir, base, history count and newest and oldest commit, jobs by state, throughput, invalid records) in snapshot.rs. Its display is `display::snapshot_status`, and the throughput block is `Throughput::text()`, printed the same way as display.rs 1076-1078.
decisions.reason: It gives the producer and verifier what real-records checks need without a repository. status.rs is already 142 KB, so the new code goes in snapshot.rs; status.rs gets only the parity test.

rejected.why: It would touch every consumer of `StatusView` and its JSON.

decisions.choice: Planner, critic and reader briefs are not changed.
decisions.reason: The criteria name only the producer and verifier briefs. The reader, planner and critic get a plain copy without records (system-facts). `planning.rs`, `admission.rs` and `refusal_corpus.rs` change only to add `evidence: None` to existing `Policy` literals.

rejected.why: Beyond the criteria, and it would widen the sandbox for roles that do not run commands.

risks.risk: The immutable attribute (`chattr +i`) may not hold on the CI or sandbox file system, so dispatch would fail there.
risks.mitigation: The lock probes writes and fails dispatch loudly when the lock does not hold (it never silently skips), the same as the verifier's lock, which existing tests already depend on. The error text tells the user to run as a user the bits bind, or on a file system that supports the immutable attribute.

risks.risk: The Claude host may ignore `--add-dir`, or reject it, under `--restricted`. Agents would then be unable to read the evidence despite the hook allowing it.
risks.mitigation: `--add-dir` is added only when `read_dirs` is non-empty (producer and verifier with an evidence dir). The open question flags it for the user. The brief section tells agents the tools to use, and `athena status --snapshot` via `cargo run` stays reachable because cargo arguments are not path-confined.

risks.risk: The read exemption could widen the sandbox, for example by symlink tricks or a sibling directory sharing the prefix.
risks.mitigation: `confine` resolves symlinks and `..` first (policy.rs 406-425) and compares to the canonicalized evidence root with `starts_with` on path components. The exemption applies only when `write` is false. Tests cover `..`, symlink escape, the `evidence-other` sibling, and write and redirect denial.

risks.risk: The `Records::load` refactor changes behavior for every caller.
risks.mitigation: Keep `from_parts` as the only assembly path. `load` keeps its landing sort and dedup. The parity test compares full throughput text on records with landings in both the tree and (where the fixture supports it) the records-branch tip.

risks.risk: The copy of a large `records/` directory costs disk and time on every dispatch.
risks.mitigation: The copy is raw blob bytes, with no parsing, written after the disk gates. Only `records/` and `landings/` are copied, not the repo. The size is not measured here (an estimate: small next to a build).

risks.risk: A longer producer brief could hit a size or token limit.
risks.mitigation: Section text is short, added only with evidence, and the frames are not touched. The existing size-cap test (briefs.rs ~3767) compares the diff-inlining cases and is rerun by criterion 5.

risks.risk: A resumed or retried dispatch finds an old locked evidence dir.
risks.mitigation: Dispatch is retried with `athena retry`; `snapshot::write` removes any earlier evidence dir through `remove_tree` (unlock first) before copying. The test covers a rewrite.

risks.risk: The real state path could reach a committed record through a command line or brief.
risks.mitigation: The producer's `commands_run` are redacted with `<state>` already (lib.rs `redactor`). Stored briefs hold the placeholder, and a test asserts the temp path is absent from `brief-producer.md` and `brief-verifier.md`.

demonstrations.observes: Seen from inside the producer invocation: the directory at the named path exists; creating a new file and opening an existing file for write both fail; `records/` bytes equal `git show <head>:records/...` for every file; and `history.json` has the dispatch base as `base`, the first commit's hash equal to `git rev-parse <base>`, its subject, a committer time, and the `Athena-Job` trailer of the ask commit. The committed `brief-producer.md` contains `<state>/jobs/<id>/evidence` and not the temp directory path, and the verifier prompt (captured the same way) names the real path. `snapshot::tests` covers unlocked write succeeds then locked write fails, the 200-commit cap, and rewriting over an existing locked evidence dir.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the dispatch step the evidence dir does not exist at the path the producer prompt names, and the probe's reads and history assertions fail. Without `lock` the in-script write succeeds as root, so the 'write attempt fails' assertion fails; the unit test first shows the write works on the unlocked copy. If the lock cannot hold, `snapshot::write` returns an error and dispatch fails. The test fails; it never skips.

demonstrations.method: In status.rs tests, build a scratch git repo from the existing `timed_job` records (several landed jobs and failed ones), plus landing records written as `HistoryRecord::Landing` JSON under `landings/`, using the existing `landing_of` helper. Commit it. Compute `Throughput::compute(&Records::load(&git, "HEAD")).text()`. Then `snapshot::write` to a temp dir and call `snapshot::status(dir)` (the function behind `athena status --snapshot`) and compare `view.throughput.text()` byte for byte.
demonstrations.observes: The two throughput texts are identical and contain the landing-record basis line. The record count and the invalid list also match.
demonstrations.fails_without: If `from_parts` were not shared, or `landings/` were not copied (or the records-branch tip's landings dropped), the snapshot's throughput text would differ: window_with_landing_record would drop and the text would say 'no landing record (landings/) found'. The test fails on text inequality, and it also asserts the text contains 'landing record (landings/) found for each' so an empty comparison cannot pass.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry points: `Records::load` (store.rs 311) and `snapshot::write` / `snapshot::status` (step 3). The fixture is a temp git repo, with a tempdir for the snapshot. Records come from the existing `timed_job` and `landing_of` helpers in status.rs tests (3150-3357), which exist today. No double is involved; both sides are real code over real files. The test is added in step 12.

demonstrations.method: Use the lifecycle pattern (lifecycle.rs 204-223): `Fixture::new()`, `athena.ask`, `athena.go` with the fake driver, so a job lands. Call `athena_core::snapshot::write(&fx.git, &fx.head(), dir)`. Run the real binary `athena status --snapshot <dir> --json` with the cwd set to an empty temp dir (assert it has no `records/` and no `.git`) and HOME pointed at a temp dir. Also run it without `--json` and with a missing dir.
demonstrations.observes: The exit code is 0. The JSON `jobs_by_state` and `throughput` equal those of `fx.athena(..).status()` (serialized values). The plain output contains `Throughput::text()` of that view and the history summary. A missing snapshot dir exits non-zero with a message naming the dir. A `--snapshot` run together with a job argument is refused by clap (`conflicts_with`).
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the `--snapshot` option clap rejects the argument and the exit is non-zero. If it called `open()` it would fail with no repository in the cwd. If it read cwd records it would find none. A decoy assertion (snapshot of a repo with one landed job; cwd with an empty `records/`-less temp dir) shows the output matches the snapshot's data.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry point: the `athena` binary (`env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_athena")`, as in binary.rs and common::athena_check, which exist) through `Command::Status { snapshot }`. Fixture: common::Fixture and Scenario (exist). The binary is run as a child process with `current_dir` set to a temp dir. The new test file crates/athena-cli/tests/status_snapshot.rs is added in step 13.

demonstrations.method: In briefs.rs tests, build the existing `producer_inputs(None)` and `plain_verifier_inputs()` and call `producer_brief_with_evidence(.., Some("<state>/jobs/<id>/evidence"))` and `verifier_brief_with_evidence(..)`.
demonstrations.observes: Each brief contains the path, the phrase that real-records checks use the evidence snapshot read-only (also `history.json` and `athena status --snapshot <path>`), and still contains 'records/, the owner's private files, and history are absent by design' for the working copy. With None, the output equals the old functions' output.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the evidence section the producer and verifier briefs do not contain the path or the real-records sentence, so both tests fail. If the working-copy sentence were removed or records/ implied, the 'still absent' assertions fail. A third test shows the briefs without an evidence argument are byte-identical to `producer_brief` and `verifier_brief_with_plan`.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry points: `producer_brief_with_evidence` and `verifier_brief_with_evidence` (step 6), reached by `producer_brief` and `verifier_brief_with_plan`, which delegate. demonstrations.observes: A new bullet under `## [Unreleased]` / `### Added` (CHANGELOG.md lines 8-21) describing the read-only evidence snapshot written at dispatch (records/, landings/, history.json under the job's state dir, named in the producer and verifier briefs) and `athena status --snapshot <dir>`.

demonstrations.method: Read `git diff --stat` and `git diff` for protected paths and for machine-specific strings.
demonstrations.observes: The stat lists no athena.toml, defaults.toml, .github/workflows/*, records/**, and no change to `Throughput::compute`, `Throughput::text` or the status.rs throughput helpers (status.rs changes are inside `#[cfg(test)]` only). Added lines hold no absolute home or state paths: tests use tempdirs and briefs use `<state>`. No email-like text.
demonstrations.fails_without: A listed protected file or a machine path would show in the stat or in a diff grep.
